front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The enthalpy change of hydration is always exothermic.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Hydration enthalpies are always exothermic because energy is released when ion-dipole bonds form between the ions and polar water molecules.

front_blocks.md: What type of bonds form between water molecules and ions during hydration, and which part of the water molecule is attracted to cations?

back_blocks.md: **Ion-dipole bonds** form during hydration. The δ<sup>-</sup> oxygen atom of water is attracted to positive ions (**cations**). The δ<sup>+</sup> hydrogen atoms are attracted to negative ions (**anions**).

front_blocks.md: Why is a negative sign placed in front of Δ*H*<sub>latt</sub><sup>θ</sup> in the energy cycle equation?

back_blocks.md: Lattice energy (Δ*H*<sub>latt</sub><sup>θ</sup>) refers to lattice formation. In the energy cycle, the lattice is being broken (dissociated), which is the reverse process, so a negative sign is used. This is sometimes referred to as **lattice dissociation enthalpy**.

front_blocks.md: Explain why the enthalpy of hydration of Mg<sup>2+</sup> is more exothermic than that of Ba<sup>2+</sup>.

back_blocks.md: Mg<sup>2+</sup> has a smaller **ionic radius** than Ba<sup>2+</sup>, giving it a higher **charge density**. This leads to stronger **ion-dipole attractions** with water molecules and more energy released during hydration.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Higher ionic charge leads to less exothermic hydration enthalpies.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Higher ionic charge leads to greater charge density, which strengthens ion-dipole attractions with water molecules and makes hydration enthalpies more exothermic.

front_blocks.md: The enthalpy of hydration of CaO is more exothermic than that of KCl because Ca<sup>2+</sup> and O<sup>2-</sup> have **..........**  ionic charges and **..........**  ionic radii than K<sup>+</sup> and Cl<sup>-</sup>.

back_blocks.md: The enthalpy of hydration of CaO is more exothermic than that of KCl because Ca<sup>2+</sup> and O<sup>2-</sup> have **higher** ionic charges and **smaller** ionic radii than K<sup>+</sup> and Cl<sup>-</sup>.

front_blocks.md: Which ion has the more exothermic enthalpy of hydration: Mg<sup>2+</sup> or Ca<sup>2+</sup>? Give a reason.

back_blocks.md: Mg<sup>2+</sup> has the more exothermic enthalpy of hydration. It has a smaller **ionic radius** than Ca<sup>2+</sup>, giving it a higher **charge density** and stronger **ion-dipole attractions** with water molecules.

front_blocks.md: Why are hydration enthalpies always exothermic?

back_blocks.md: Energy is released when **ion-dipole bonds** form between the ions and the **polar water molecules** during hydration. Bond formation always releases energy.
